records.title: securing-mechanism-creates-cross-context-correlator

proposition.statement: A relying system must not assert cross-context unlinkability merely because the disclosed credential payload lacks a stable identifier when proof values, verification-method references, timestamps, or other securing metadata remain linkable across interactions.

preconditions: Credential or presentation payload data is intended to avoid or minimize stable cross-context identifiers.
The securing mechanism or its metadata is visible to more than one relying context.
The privacy claim depends on interactions remaining unlinkable or not readily correlatable.

trigger.statement: A verifier, colluding verifiers, or another observer can link otherwise separate interactions using stable or distinctive securing-mechanism data while the system still reports the intended privacy property as satisfied.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence describing the securing mechanism and which proof, key-reference, timestamp, or related values are exposed in each interaction.
Cross-context observations sufficient to test whether securing metadata creates a stable or probabilistic join.
Evidence identifying which component or authority generated the correlating proof material or metadata.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS for unlinkability while repeated or otherwise distinctive proof metadata links interactions across contexts.
Privacy analysis inspects only the credential payload and excludes observable securing-mechanism metadata that materially enables correlation.

records.title: status-resolution-exposes-presentation-activity

proposition.statement: A relying system must not treat a status or revocation check as privacy-neutral when the act, target, timing, or requesting context of resolution allows an issuer, status provider, or observer to infer credential presentation activity or relationships.

preconditions: A relying party resolves credential, authorization, revocation, or lifecycle status through an observable service or interaction.
The privacy objective requires limiting issuer or status-provider knowledge of where or when a credential is used.
The status result itself may be minimal and semantically correct.

trigger.statement: The status-resolution event exposes a credential-specific or context-specific observation that permits usage correlation, while the verification flow still treats privacy assurance as satisfied.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence describing which parties can observe status-resolution requests and what relationship information those observations reveal.
Evidence of request timing and whether timing can be associated with a presentation or relying-party event.
Cross-context observations sufficient to test whether status-resolution activity creates a join between otherwise separate interactions.
Evidence identifying the status source and any intermediaries able to observe the request.

falsification.condition: The system reports PASS for the privacy proposition even though the status provider can associate credential-specific requests with distinct presentation events.
Assessment examines only the content of the status response and ignores privacy-significant metadata created by making the lookup.

records.title: legitimate-disclosure-reused-beyond-relying-purpose

proposition.statement: A successful and initially legitimate disclosure must not be treated as continuing permission to retain, transfer, profile, resell, or otherwise process the disclosed information beyond the purpose, audience, retention period, or governance basis applicable to the relying transaction.

preconditions: The holder or subject legitimately disclosed information for a stated relying purpose.
The initial presentation or verification completed successfully.
A later processing action is materially different from or extends beyond the original relying transaction.

trigger.statement: A downstream party performs secondary processing and relies on the fact of successful presentation rather than establishing an applicable purpose, policy, authority, or other governance basis for that later use.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence of the purpose, audience, retention, transfer, and secondary-use rules governing the original disclosure and the later processing action.
Evidence distinguishing the original disclosure time from later retention, transfer, profiling, or reuse.
Evidence identifying the actor and processing chain responsible for the secondary use.

falsification.condition: The system treats successful presentation as sufficient basis for materially different downstream processing without evaluating the applicable purpose or policy.
Data is retained or transferred beyond an applicable bound while the decision record continues to represent the processing as within the original relying purpose.

records.title: authoritative-participant-defeats-intended-unlinkability

proposition.statement: A relying system must not assert an unlinkability or minimization property without testing whether identifiers, proof configuration, issuance cadence, renewal behavior, or other metadata controlled by an authoritative participant can recreate a cross-context correlator.

preconditions: The system claims or relies on a privacy property that interactions should remain unlinkable or minimally correlatable.
An issuer, registry, operator, or other authoritative participant controls metadata or lifecycle behavior visible across interactions.
The controlled values or behavior are not independently shown to preserve the declared privacy property.

trigger.statement: Authoritative participant choices create a stable or distinctive join across interactions while local credential and proof validation continue to succeed.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence identifying which participant controls each potentially correlating identifier, metadata field, proof choice, issuance event, or renewal behavior.
Cross-context evidence testing whether the combined issuer- or operator-controlled surfaces enable correlation.
Evidence defining the unlinkability or minimization property that the deployment claims to provide.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS for unlinkability while issuer-controlled or operator-controlled metadata consistently links otherwise separate interactions.
Assessment assumes that an authoritative participant preserves privacy merely because that participant is authorized to issue or operate the relevant component.

records.title: individually-minimal-disclosures-compose-into-identification

proposition.statement: A relying system must not infer that a combined disclosure is privacy-minimal merely because each credential, attribute, proof, or metadata element is individually non-identifying or independently justified when their composition enables identification, profiling, or sensitive inference.

preconditions: Multiple attributes, credentials, proofs, or metadata elements are disclosed or observable in the same or linkable relying context.
Each element is individually considered acceptable or minimally disclosing.
The combined set has not been shown to preserve the intended privacy or non-identification property.

trigger.statement: The combined disclosure set materially narrows identity, enables profiling, or reveals a sensitive inference while the system treats independent minimization of each element as sufficient privacy evidence.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence evaluating the disclosure set as a whole, including joins among attributes, credentials, proofs, metadata, and external context available to the relying party.
Evidence defining the privacy, minimization, or non-identification property expected for the combined interaction.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS for minimization solely because each disclosed element is individually justified while their combination materially enables identification or profiling.
Privacy analysis omits readily available joins among disclosed facts that change the sensitivity or identifiability of the combined result.

records.title: retained-verification-artefacts-create-durable-correlation-surface

proposition.statement: A relying system must not treat verification evidence retention as privacy-neutral when presentations, status observations, transcripts, identifiers, or related artefacts are retained or aggregated beyond the minimum justified purpose and thereby enable later cross-context reconstruction or sensitive inference.

preconditions: Verification, assurance, audit, or operational processing produces artefacts that can be persisted.
The retained artefacts contain or can be joined through identifiers, timing, proof data, status observations, or contextual metadata.
The applicable purpose does not positively establish the necessity of indefinite or broadly aggregated retention.

trigger.statement: Verification artefacts are persisted or aggregated beyond the justified purpose or retention boundary and become a durable dataset from which otherwise separate interactions can be reconstructed or correlated.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence defining the operational, assurance, audit, legal, or governance purpose and retention bound applicable to each retained artefact.
Evidence identifying which verifier, processor, repository, or evidence service retains and aggregates the artefacts.
Evidence testing whether retained artefacts can be joined across interactions or contexts to create a material correlation or inference surface.
Evidence of retention duration, expiry, deletion, and any later reuse of the retained artefacts.

falsification.condition: The system reports PASS for privacy while retaining verification artefacts beyond the established purpose or retention boundary and those artefacts permit cross-context reconstruction.
Audit or assurance value is asserted as a blanket justification for retaining raw or linkable artefacts when less correlating evidence would satisfy the same stated purpose.
